17: # Agent Reach
18: 
19: One command for every platform: `agent-reach`. Read-only; prints one JSON object by default.
20: 
21: Before acting, say "using the agent-reach skill (channel X)". Once invoked, these rules apply for the whole session.
22: 
23: ## Choosing a route
24: 
25: - For public content, use your own search/read tools first (optionally `site:domain`). Check body text, comments and subtitles separately; when they are enough, answer directly without adding channels or logging in.
26: - Use Reach when your tools are unavailable, the result lacks what the user needs, or the user wants a site action a channel declares. Unsure of actions and params? Run `agent-reach channels`.
27: - An added channel (a default one, or one added with `add`) sends search/read straight to its site tool. For channels not added yet, search/read first try anonymous public web access; results mark it with `backend: public-web`. `--backend public-web` limits to public web; `--backend <backend>` picks a site tool.
28: - A platform name or link only identifies the source; it never triggers install or login by itself.
29: - Snippets, page shells, comment counts and subtitle track lists are not body text, comments or subtitles; say which you have. If the user skips login, still deliver the public results already gathered.
30: 
31: ```bash
32: agent-reach channels                      # actions and params per channel
33: agent-reach <channel> <action> [args]     # e.g. agent-reach bilibili search "rust async" --limit 5
34: agent-reach read <url>                    # picks the channel from the URL
35: ```
36: 
37: ## Results and errors
38: 
39: - `ok: true` → content in `items`; each has `title / url / author / published_at / text`, upstream data in `raw`.
40: - `ok: false` → branch on `error.code` and follow `error.hint`:
41: 
42: | error.code | What to do |
43: |---|---|
44: | `NEED_SETUP` | Missing dependency or key. Run `agent-reach add <channel>` as hinted; for a key, the user provides it, then `agent-reach configure <key>` |
45: | `NEED_LOGIN` | Keep existing results and tell the user login is needed; `agent-reach login <channel>` opens the browser and the user logs in themselves. Never log in for them or ask for a password |
46: | `UPSTREAM_BROKEN` | This platform is temporarily not working; `message` is what was reported. Tell the user which platform is unavailable and roughly why, by platform name, without naming tools; run `agent-reach update` once, after they agree, only if the message points to an outdated tool; never retry in a loop |
47: | `TIMEOUT` | Check the failed stage and channel status (`agent-reach doctor --text`); do not retry or reopen windows in a loop |
48: | `RATE_LIMITED` | The platform rate-limited; Reach paused the channel. Wait `retry_after_seconds`; do not switch backends |
49: | `PLATFORM_BLOCKED` | The platform wants verification (captcha/risk check). Stop; the user resolves it on the official page. Do not switch accounts or backends |
50: | `BUSY` | The browser stayed full for the 2-minute wait in line, or the user has a login window open. Retry later, or after the user says they are logged in; do not close the window or switch profiles |
51: | `NOT_FOUND` | Content does not exist; check the link or ID |
52: | `BAD_INPUT` | Wrong arguments; run `agent-reach channels` for usage |
53: 
54: On `PLATFORM_BLOCKED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `NEED_LOGIN` or `BUSY`, stop this attempt; do not retry with other accounts, backends or browsers. A network failure or a failure on one machine does not mean "the platform requires login".
55: 
56: ## Login and the dedicated browser
57: 
58: All browser channels share one dedicated browser (CloakBrowser preferred, falling back to installed Chrome). It runs headless by default, closes after 10 idle minutes and reopens on the next call. Calls may run in parallel, including from subagents: up to 2 per platform and 4 in total run at once, the rest wait in line, and two searches on the same platform start at least 10 seconds apart.
59: 
60: The first time a site is used, if the user's Chrome is connected to the OpenCLI extension, that site's login is copied once into the dedicated browser and reused afterwards; only that site is copied and the source browser is untouched. Only when the login has expired or there is no source to copy from does the user run `agent-reach login <channel>` and log in themselves. Refreshing, choosing a source and logging out are in [Sessions](references/sessions.md): read it when the user wants to log in, log out or switch accounts, or on `NEED_LOGIN`.
61: 
62: ## Platform notes
63: 
64: - Xiaohongshu read returns text descriptions only; never claim to understand the images or video.
65: - When a Boss Zhipin search result has `salary_encoded=true`, never guess the salary digits; read the job link for the readable salary in the detail.
66: - What each platform offers publicly and what Reach adds is in [Capability scope](references/capabilities.md): read it when the user asks "what can it get / is it complete" or you need to judge completeness.
67: 
68: ## Channels
69: 
70: | channel | level | actions | login |
71: |---|---|---|---|
72: | github | default | search, read | - |
73: | twitter | experimental | search, profile, tweets, thread | `agent-reach login twitter` |
74: | youtube | default | read, search, subtitle, transcribe | - |
75: | reddit | optional | search, read, subreddit | Browser path only, if required |
76: | facebook | experimental | search, profile | `agent-reach login facebook` |
77: | instagram | experimental | search, profile, posts | `agent-reach login instagram` |
78: | bilibili | default | search, read, hot, subtitle | `agent-reach login bilibili` |
79: | xiaohongshu | optional | search, read, comments | `agent-reach login xiaohongshu` |
80: | linkedin | optional | jobs, read | `agent-reach login linkedin` |
81: | boss | optional | search, read | `agent-reach login boss` |
82: | v2ex | default | hot, node, read, user | - |
83: | xueqiu | optional | quote, search, hot_posts, hot_stocks | `agent-reach login xueqiu` |
84: | xiaoyuzhou | optional | transcribe | - |
85: | web | default | search, read | - |
86: 
87: `default` channels are installed by default and can be removed; updates never add a removed one back. The `login` column is the authentication entry point, not a prerequisite for public content.
88: 
89: ## After installation
90: 
91: After `agent-reach setup`, show `result.installation_report.markdown` to the user as is: no additions, removals, reordering, extra greeting or tables. The program generates it.
92: 
93: ## When the user wants to manage Agent Reach
94: 
95: | User says | You run |
96: |---|---|
97: | Add a platform | `agent-reach add <channel>`; dependencies install automatically. Tell the user only what they must do (log in or provide a key) |
98: | Remove a platform | `agent-reach remove <channel>` |
99: | Log in / login expired | `agent-reach login <channel>`; the user logs in themselves in the window that opens |
100: | Log out | `agent-reach logout <channel>` |
101: | Status / what works | `agent-reach doctor --text`; for a live test `agent-reach check <channel> --text` |
102: | Upgrade / update | `agent-reach update` |
103: | Uninstall | show `agent-reach uninstall --dry-run` first, then `agent-reach uninstall` once they confirm |
104: | Another AI should use it | `agent-reach skill link <that AI's skills folder>`; `agent-reach skill` shows where it is placed now |
105: 
106: Troubleshooting, browser maintenance and uninstall details are in [Maintenance](references/maintenance.md): read it when an update fails, the browser will not start, or the user wants to uninstall.
107: 
108: ## When there is a new version
109: 
110: Any result with `meta.update` means a newer version exists. Mention it once per conversation, in the user's language and plain words:
111: 
112: 1. Agent Reach has a new version (`meta.update.latest`).
113: 2. What changed: 1 to 3 short points from `meta.update.notes`.
114: 3. Ask whether to update; run `agent-reach update` only after the user agrees.
115: 
116: ## Red lines
117: 
118: - Read only. Never post, comment, like or message.
119: - Never log in for the user; never ask for or print passwords, cookies or other credentials.
120: - Ordinary queries never change dependencies or update automatically.

### injector

Inject code before or after your solution, injected code won't be submitted or run.

Imports will be injected at the top of the buffer, automatically
folded by default.

```lua
injector = { ---@type table<lc.lang, lc.inject>
    ["python3"] = {
        imports = function(default_imports)
            vim.list_extend(default_imports, { "from .leetcode import *" })
            return default_imports
        end,
        after = { "def test():", "    print('test')" },
    },
    ["cpp"] = {
        imports = function()
            -- return a different list to omit default imports
            return { "#include <bits/stdc++.h>", "using namespace std;" }
        end,
        after = "int main() {}",
    },
},
```

### picker

Supported picker providers are:

- [`snacks-picker`][snacks.nvim]
- [`fzf-lua`][fzf-lua]
- [`telescope`][telescope.nvim]

picker = { provider = nil },

## 📋 Commands

### `Leet` opens menu dashboard

- `menu` same as `Leet`

- `exit` close [leetcode.nvim]

- `console` opens console pop-up for currently opened question

- `info` opens a pop-up containing information about the currently opened question

- `tabs` opens a picker with all currently opened question tabs

- `yank` yanks the code section

- `lang` opens a picker to change the language of the current question

- `run` run currently opened question

- `test` same as `Leet run`

- `submit` submit currently opened question

- `random` opens a random question

- `daily` opens the question of today problem

- `list` opens a picker with all available leetcode problems

- `open` opens the current question in a default browser

- `restore` try to restore default question layout

- `last_submit` tries to replace the editor code section with the latest submitted code

- `reset` resets editor code section to the default snippet

- `inject` re-injects editor code, keeping the code section intact

- `fold` applies folding to the current question imports section

<!-- - `session` -->
<!--   - `create` create a new session -->
<!--   - `change` change the current session -->
<!---->

- `desc` toggle question description
  - `toggle` same as `Leet desc`

  - `stats` toggle description stats visibility

- `cookie`
  - `update` opens a prompt to enter a new cookie

  - `delete` deletes stored cookie and logs out of [leetcode.nvim]

- `cache`
  - `update` fetches all available problems and updates the local cache of [leetcode.nvim]

#### Some commands can take optional arguments. To stack argument values separate them by a `,`

- `Leet list`

  ```
  Leet list status=<status> difficulty=<difficulty>
  ```

- `Leet random`

  ```
  Leet random status=<status> difficulty=<difficulty> tags=<tags>
  ```

## 🚀 Usage

This plugin can be initiated in two ways:

- To start [leetcode.nvim], simply pass [`arg`](#arg)
  as the _first and **only**_ [Neovim] argument

  ```
  nvim leetcode.nvim
  ```

- Use `:Leet` command to open [leetcode.nvim]
  within your preferred dashboard plugin. The only requirement is that [Neovim]
  must not have any listed buffers open.
  To bypass this requirement use [`non_standalone`](#non-standalone-mode) plugin.

### Sign In

> [!WARNING]

https://github.com/kawre/leetcode.nvim/assets/69250723/b7be8b95-5e2c-4153-8845-4ad3abeda5c3

## ❓ FAQ

### I keep getting `cookie expired` error

If you keep getting `Your cookie may have expired, or LeetCode has temporarily
restricted API access`, it most likely means that LeetCode website is under
heavy load and is restricting API access (mostly during contests).

All you can do is wait it out, try disabling a VPN if you’re using one, and if
the problem is persistent, open an issue.

### Switching between test cases

To switch between test cases, just press the number of the corresponding case:  
`1` for `Case (1)`, `2` for `Case (2)`, and so on.

### Switching between questions

To switch between questions, use `Leet tabs`

### I'm not getting LSP completions

Some languages require additional setup to get LSP completions.  
For example, Rust needs extra configuration — see [this issue](https://github.com/kawre/leetcode.nvim/issues/86).

## 🍴 Recipes

### 💤 lazy loading with [lazy.nvim]

> [!WARNING]
> opting for either option makes the alternative
> launch method unavailable due to lazy loading

- with [`arg`](#arg)

  ```lua
  local leet_arg = "leetcode.nvim"
  ```

  ```lua
  {
      "kawre/leetcode.nvim",
      lazy = leet_arg ~= vim.fn.argv(0, -1),
      opts = { arg = leet_arg },
  }
  ```

- with `:Leet`

  ```lua
  {
      "kawre/leetcode.nvim",
      cmd = "Leet",
  }
  ```

### 🪟 Windows

If you are using Windows,
it is recommended to use [Cygwin](https://www.cygwin.com/) for a more consistent and Unix-like experience.

## 🧩 Plugins

### Non-Standalone mode

To run [leetcode.nvim] in a non-standalone mode (i.e. not with argument or an empty Neovim session),
enable the `non_standalone` plugin in your config:

```lua
plugins = {
    non_standalone = true,
}
```

You can then exit [leetcode.nvim] using `:Leet exit` command

local function inspect_tokens(lang, code)
    local parser = vim.treesitter.get_string_parser(code, lang)
    local tree = parser:parse()[1]
    local query = vim.treesitter.query.get(lang, 'highlights')
    if not query then
        print(lang .. ': No highlights query!')
        return
    end
    print('=== ' .. lang .. ' ===')
    local captures = {}
    for id, node, _ in query:iter_captures(tree:root(), code) do
        local name = query.captures[id]
        if not captures[name] then
            captures[name] = true
            local text = vim.treesitter.get_node_text(node, code)
            print(string.format('  @%-24s -> %q', name, text:sub(1, 20)))
        end
    end
end

### 1. Root Cause Analysis

1. **Tree-sitter Attachment & Options in [init.lua](file:///home/prem/.config/nvim/init.lua)**:
   - Tree-sitter parsers (`python`, `c`, `bash`, `lua`) and the parser attachment logic (`vim.treesitter.start(buf, language)`) were configured and attaching to buffers properly.
   - However, `vim.o.termguicolors` was missing from the base options in [init.lua](file:///home/prem/.config/nvim/init.lua#L111) (it was only invoked conditionally when the colorscheme was loaded).

2. **Colorscheme Inspection ([ravenswing.lua](file:///home/prem/.config/nvim/colors/ravenswing.lua))**:
   - The primary reason code appeared colorless was that `ravenswing.lua` was originally authored as a strict **monochrome** theme:
     - Normal text was `#BFBFBF` (`c.light`).
     - Standard groups (`String`, `Function`, `Constant`, `Number`, `Identifier`, `Boolean`) and Tree-sitter groups (`@string`, `@function`, `@variable`, `@number`, `@property`, `@constant`) were all hardcoded to the exact same `#BFBFBF`.
     - Keywords, types, comments, and operators were all set to `#7D7D7D` (`c.mid`).
     - Modern Tree-sitter capture groups (e.g., `@variable.parameter`, `@keyword.return`, `@keyword.import`, `@keyword.directive`, `@variable.member`, `@string.escape`, etc.) were missing.
     - Crucially, all `@lsp.type.*` semantic token groups (`@lsp.type.variable`, `@lsp.type.function`, `@lsp.type.parameter`, etc.) were hardcoded to `{ fg = c.light }` (`#BFBFBF`), stripping any syntax distinction whenever an LSP client was active.

#### A. Updated `ravenswing.lua` Syntax Palette
In [ravenswing.lua](file:///home/prem/.config/nvim/colors/ravenswing.lua), the theme's dark minimalist UI (pure `#000000` pitch-black background, `#2F2F2F` statusline/cursorline, subtle borders, and matching menus) was left intact. A complementary syntax palette was introduced:

| **Numbers & Floats** | `@number`, `@number.float`, `Number`, `Float` | `#e0af68` | Warm Amber / Honey Gold |
| **Booleans & Constants** | `@boolean`, `@constant`, `@constant.builtin`, `Boolean` | `#ff9e64` | Sunset Peach / Coral |

#### B. Linked LSP Semantic Tokens
Replaced the flat grayscale override for LSP semantic tokens by linking `@lsp.type.*` captures directly to their corresponding Tree-sitter groups (`@lsp.type.function` $\rightarrow$ `@function`, `@lsp.type.parameter` $\rightarrow$ `@variable.parameter`, etc.). When language servers attach, semantic tokens preserve and enhance highlighting.

Added `vim.o.termguicolors = true` to [init.lua#L111](file:///home/prem/.config/nvim/init.lua#L111) to guarantee 24-bit true color initialization from startup.
